text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Thursday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- Newspaper sources said that the temporary administrator of Innovation Bank, Romualdas Visokavichius, might be appointed the new head of Lithuanian Savings Bank. Finance Minister Algirdas Shemeta said earlier that changes are pending in the managment of the state-run bank.
- Health care minister Juozas Galdikas expects that the new health insurance law will come into effect on July 1.
- Thomson BankWatch granted a BB credit rating to Lithuania, Vilniaus Bank and Hermis Bank, one notch higher than the previous rating.
- The Lithuanian government failed to reach an agreement on issuing state guarantees for $200 million in credits for the building of the Butinge oil terminal.
- The conflict in the ministry of culture continues and four more experts resigned in protest at the administrative style of the minister, Saulius Shaltenis. Three vice ministers resigned earlier.
- The Bank of Lithuania is to decide whether to extend the term of its 13.7 million million litas loan to Tauras Bank.
- Security Department officials siezed the last parts of a cassette with 50 kilograms of radioactive uranium stolen from Ignalina nuclear power plant. A numer of suspects have been detained.
- The prime ministers of the three Baltic countries intend to issue a joint-statement in Tallinn today ezpressing their readiness to join the EU.
